scope: Independent source and evidence review of the bounded exact Number sine/cosine reduction and primitive integer dispatch. No production code changes made during review.
checks: The half-pi constant is the exact original 66-bit dyadic, split into a 53-bit high component and an exact at-most-13-bit low component; binary64 pi is not substituted.

The [.5,2^20] domain bounds the integer quotient to 20 bits and the low-component product to 33 bits. The reduction and quarter-boundary comparisons fit exact two-component dyadics with support between exponents -66 and 21; no intermediate approaches overflow or underflow.

Quarter-boundary correction follows the original signed division tie convention, and the final closed-interval guard declines any unsupported quotient. Small polynomial inputs and ambiguous final m80 rounding retain the unchanged original reduction/series path.

The direct Number path reuses the existing certified anchored polynomial and preserves its conservative interval radius. Control-word changes clear the private bounded Number cache, signed zeros bypass its merged-zero key, and its wrapper is private and immutable.

The source-pinned 100000-case reducer diagnostic reconstructs the exact original fixed224 input/quadrant and compares each accepted DD sum exactly, including neighboring binary64 quarter-boundary values; its sampled final results compare with the committed original series at all three precision words.

Primitive integer dispatch preserves strict DWORD conversion and integer-origin zero semantics. Independent differential checks cover truthy/falsy/changing/throwing Number.prototype.events getters and compare outputs, exceptions and ordered getter receiver values against 15fd6ac.
limitations: The reduction corpus is supporting evidence rather than an exhaustive proof of all binary64 inputs. Native integration and browser pace are recorded separately; this review does not claim native vendor transcendental polynomials are reproduced outside the existing simulator translation.
